purpose: Reusable source-backed organ-function, special-population, and high-risk safety knowledge for evaluation and case generation. General regulatory guidance defines evidence structure; product-specific management still requires a current label/guideline.
principles: General renal/hepatic guidance is methodology truth, not a patient-specific dose engine.
Pregnancy/lactation labeling must preserve current PLLR narrative semantics rather than obsolete letter categories.
Risk/warning relations must not be silently upgraded to diagnosis or universal management rules.
Product-specific label claims remain formulation/version scoped.

modules.forbidden_inference: Do not treat an obsolete pregnancy letter category as current FDA risk truth or convert pregnancy exposure into an automatic contraindication without product-specific evidence.

modules.title: Lactation labeling under PLLR
modules.forbidden_inference: Drug presence in milk does not by itself prove infant harm; absence of data does not prove safety.

modules.title: Sertraline / serotonin syndrome warning

claims.subject: serotonin syndrome
claims.object: mental-status + autonomic + neuromuscular + seizure + GI findings

modules.forbidden_inference: One nonspecific symptom does not confirm serotonin syndrome; co-use of serotonergic drugs does not prove the syndrome is present.

modules.title: Glipizide severe hypoglycemia risk
modules.forbidden_inference: Glipizide exposure or a risk factor does not itself establish that the patient is currently hypoglycemic.

modules.forbidden_inference: Acetaminophen use alone does not diagnose DILI; a product warning is not an incidence estimate and remains formulation/product scoped.
